instruction: A PM flagged that {{reference-architectures-Glue-etlpipeline-us-east-1-PipelineName}} has not produced a single Glue job run since the stack shipped four days ago — the Glue console shows zero jobs and the artifact bucket is empty. We want to unblock it, but before we ship a fix we also want to know what else along the deploy path is broken or fragile, so the whole mess goes into one change. What is actually stopping this pipeline from running right now, and once that is fixed, what other problems are sitting in the wiring between the pipeline, the launcher, and the Glue job that we should be pulling into the same PR?
expected_answer:
What is blocking it right now: the Source action of {{reference-architectures-Glue-etlpipeline-us-east-1-PipelineName}} is configured with Provider=CodeCommit and BranchName=main, pointing at {{reference-architectures-Glue-etlpipeline-us-east-1-CodeCommitRepoName}}. That repository has zero branches. The stack created the repo but never seeded it with any code, so there is no main branch and no commits at all. The pipeline has exactly one execution in its history (triggered automatically by CloudFormation when the stack was first deployed), and it failed at the Source stage in about one second with ConfigurationError: no branch named main was found in the selected AWS CodeCommit repository. The EventBridge rule that would re-trigger the pipeline on a CodeCommit push only fires on referenceCreated/referenceUpdated events where referenceName is main, so until someone pushes an initial commit on a main branch, the pipeline will never start again on its own. This is why there are no Glue jobs, no artifact objects, and no Lambda log group for the launcher. None of that downstream work has ever been reached.

What else is broken in the deploy path, latent until code is pushed: two independent problems sit between the Source stage and a working Glue run, and neither will surface from pipeline status once the repo is seeded. First, the launcher Lambda that implements the Deploy action, {{reference-architectures-Glue-etlpipeline-us-east-1-LambdaFunctionName}}, runs start_job_run against Glue and then immediately calls put_job_success_result back to CodePipeline, with no get_job_run polling in between. The Deploy stage will report SUCCESS the instant the Glue job is accepted, regardless of whether the Glue job itself fails, times out, or produces garbage. Pipeline green will not mean ETL green. Second, the Glue worker role (passed in the launcher's UserParameters alongside {{reference-architectures-Glue-etlpipeline-us-east-1-GlueJobName}}) has no AWSGlueServiceRole managed policy attached (list-attached-role-policies returns an empty list), and its single inline policy only grants glue:CreateJob/StartJobRun on the job, KMS on the pipeline key, and S3 read/write on the pipeline artifact bucket. There are no logs:CreateLogGroup/CreateLogStream/PutLogEvents permissions anywhere on that role, and no cloudwatch:PutMetricData. The two glue:* actions that are there are actually caller-side actions and belong on the launcher Lambda, not on the worker role. Once the repo is seeded and the Lambda finally fires, the Glue job will start, fail when it tries to write to its CloudWatch log group, and, because of the fire-and-forget launcher above, the pipeline will still report Deploy SUCCESS, with the only real failure signal being the JobRunState on the Glue job itself. All three fixes belong in the same PR: seed the repo with an initial main commit that includes the ETL script, change the launcher to poll get_job_run (or use the CodePipeline Lambda continuation token) before reporting success, and attach AWSGlueServiceRole (or at minimum the necessary logs:* permissions) to the GlueRole.
